events.body:
C1: The driver cancelled as a rider no-show, but the GPS record shows he was inside the 200 m pickup radius for only 2 min 50 s before cancelling — less than the more-than-3-minutes wait NS-1 (iii) requires. [F2 F5 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C2: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:29:10 and cancelled at 21:30:55, so he stayed within the pickup radius for only 1 min 45 s after his own arrival tap — also short of the 3-minute threshold. [F6 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C3: The rider was charged the $6.61 cancellation fee (F7) even though NS-1's waiting-time condition fails, so under NS-2 the whole fee must be refunded to the rider. [F7 F4 F2] [NS-2 NS-0 NS-7]
C4: The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited at least 5 minutes" (F12) is contradicted by the system records: he was stationary only 2 min 5 s (21:28:50–21:30:55) and within 200 m for only 2 min 50 s before cancelling, so the statement cannot be relied on. [F12 F3 F2] [NS-1]
C5: The driver cancelled the trip himself at 21:30:55, 4 min 55 s after acceptance, without the rider no-show conditions being met, so the fee was not validly incurred and is chargeable to the rider at all — nothing in the record shows the rider cancelled. [F4 F5] [NS-0 NS-2 NS-3]
C6: No traffic or weather cause is recorded for the short stop-and-cancel (no incidents, no congestion bands, fair weather), so the cancellation cannot be justified by any external obstruction. [F13 F14 F15] [NS-1 NS-2]

C8: The chat shows the driver's own message timed 21:29 saying he had just arrived and a second at 21:30 saying he was cancelling because he "waited too long" — barely one minute after announcing his arrival, which is inconsistent with the 3-minute wait the policy requires. [F9 F10 F11] [NS-1 NS-2]
Weaknesses: The driver did press "I'm Here" (F6), so the NS-1 (i) condition is satisfied; our case rests entirely on the waiting-duration condition (iii), and the judge may read the 21:28:05 arrival to 21:30:55 cancellation gap (F5) as close to a 3-minute wait — the system's 2 min 50 s within-200 m figure (F2) is what defeats it. | The driver's written statement claims a 5-minute wait (F12); although it is contradicted by the GPS timeline (F3, F2), a judge weighing the driver's account could disagree about how the wait is measured from the first approach rather than the arrival tap. | We rely on profile facts (F17) only as an additional flag_account request; the two prior upheld no-show disputes concern other trips and cannot establish that this particular cancellation was improper.
Asks: refund_full $6.61

The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited at least 5 minutes" (F12) is contradicted by the system records: he was stationary only 2 min 5 s (21:28:50–21:30:55) and within 200 m for only 2 min 50 s before cancelling, so the statement cannot be relied on.

The driver cancelled the trip himself at 21:30:55, 4 min 55 s after acceptance, without the rider no-show conditions being met, so the fee was not validly incurred and is chargeable to the rider at all — nothing in the record shows the rider cancelled.
No traffic or weather cause is recorded for the short stop-and-cancel (no incidents, no congestion bands, fair weather), so the cancellation cannot be justified by any external obstruction.

The driver's 90-day record shows 2 no-show disputes, both upheld, and 451 trips — this supports sending his account to Ryde for review (flag_account) alongside the refund, though the pattern alone does not decide the case.

The chat shows the driver's own message timed 21:29 saying he had just arrived and a second at 21:30 saying he was cancelling because he "waited too long" — barely one minute after announcing his arrival, which is inconsistent with the 3-minute wait the policy requires.

weaknesses: The driver did press "I'm Here" (F6), so the NS-1 (i) condition is satisfied; our case rests entirely on the waiting-duration condition (iii), and the judge may read the 21:28:05 arrival to 21:30:55 cancellation gap (F5) as close to a 3-minute wait — the system's 2 min 50 s within-200 m figure (F2) is what defeats it.

The driver's written statement claims a 5-minute wait (F12); although it is contradicted by the GPS timeline (F3, F2), a judge weighing the driver's account could disagree about how the wait is measured from the first approach rather than the arrival tap.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled as a rider no-show, but the GPS record shows he was inside the 200 m pickup radius for only 2 min 50 s before cancelling — less than the more-than-3-minutes wait NS-1 (iii) requires.
The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:29:10 and cancelled at 21:30:55, so he stayed within the pickup radius for only 1 min 45 s after his own arrival tap — also short of the 3-minute threshold.
The rider was charged the $6.61 cancellation fee (F7) even though NS-1's waiting-time condition fails, so under NS-2 the whole fee must be refunded to the rider.

The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited at least 5 minutes" (F12) is contradicted by the system records: he was stationary only 2 min 5 s (21:28:50–21:30:55) and within 200 m for only 2 min 50 s before cancelling, so the statement cannot be relied on.

The driver cancelled the trip himself at 21:30:55, 4 min 55 s after acceptance, without the rider no-show conditions being met, so the fee was not validly incurred and is chargeable to the rider at all — nothing in the record shows the rider cancelled.
No traffic or weather cause is recorded for the short stop-and-cancel (no incidents, no congestion bands, fair weather), so the cancellation cannot be justified by any external obstruction.

The driver's 90-day record shows 2 no-show disputes, both upheld, and 451 trips — this supports sending his account to Ryde for review (flag_account) alongside the refund, though the pattern alone does not decide the case.

The chat shows the driver's own message timed 21:29 saying he had just arrived and a second at 21:30 saying he was cancelling because he "waited too long" — barely one minute after announcing his arrival, which is inconsistent with the 3-minute wait the policy requires.

weaknesses: The driver did press "I'm Here" (F6), so the NS-1 (i) condition is satisfied; our case rests entirely on the waiting-duration condition (iii), and the judge may read the 21:28:05 arrival to 21:30:55 cancellation gap (F5) as close to a 3-minute wait — the system's 2 min 50 s within-200 m figure (F2) is what defeats it.

The driver's written statement claims a 5-minute wait (F12); although it is contradicted by the GPS timeline (F3, F2), a judge weighing the driver's account could disagree about how the wait is measured from the first approach rather than the arrival tap.

We rely on profile facts (F17) only as an additional flag_account request; the two prior upheld no-show disputes concern other trips and cannot establish that this particular cancellation was improper.

claims.assertion: The driver did reach the pick-up point: GPS shows his closest approach to the pickup was 38 m at 21:30:00 (F1), and the platform itself recorded his arrival at 21:28:05 (F5), so he was physically at the designated location per GPS data.
The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 21:29:10 while only 42 m from the pickup point and remained within 200 m for 1 min 45 s after the tap (F6), so requirement (i) of NS-1 is satisfied.

The driver informed the rider in-app at 21:29 with his exact location and vehicle: "I'm here, silver Toyota Altis." (F9), and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped (F11), so the arrival notice is documented.

The driver's honoured waiting time fell 11 seconds short of the 3-minute threshold: cumulative time within 200 m of pickup before cancellation was 2 min 50 s (F2) and he cancelled at 21:30:55, 2 min 50 s after the recorded arrival of 21:28:05 (F5, F4). On the system records, NS-1(iii) is therefore not literally met.

Because the 3-minute condition is not satisfied on the records, NS-2 directs that the $6.61 cancellation fee be refunded in full to the rider; the driver acknowledges this and asks the tribunal to record it as a good-faith no-show attempt rather than an abuse of the button.
The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited at least 5 minutes" (F12) is contradicted by GPS/timeline records (F2, F5, F6) and must be disregarded in favour of the system record.

No fraud-based account flag is warranted here: the driver was genuinely within 200 m (F1, F2) and did press "I'm Here" at the pickup (F6), so the NS-2 flag condition (tapping "I'm Here" while GPS shows the driver away from the pickup) is not met.
The rider was charged the $6.61 cancellation fee (F7) with no surge applied (F8), so the refund amount is exactly $6.61 as recorded in the fare facts.

There are no safety issues in this case: the chat contains only a location notice and a cancellation notice (F9, F10), weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F15), and no traffic incident or congestion record exists (F13, F14), so no escalation under SAFE-1/SAFE-2 arises.

weaknesses: The hard record defeats the driver's no-show defence: cumulative within-200 m time was only 2 min 50 s (F2) and cancellation came 2 min 50 s after recorded arrival (F5) — 11 seconds short of the 3:01 required by NS-1(iii), so NS-2 mandates a full refund.
The rider will rely on F5 and F2 to show the driver cancelled before the 3-minute wait elapsed, and on the rider's own clean profile (F16, 0 disputes in 90 days) to look credible.

The driver's own written statement claiming a 5-minute wait (F12) is directly contradicted by F2/F5 and will be used to attack his credibility (G11-adjacent: his uncorroborated assertion is a claim, not evidence).

The driver's profile (F17: 2 no-show disputes, both upheld in 90 days) gives the rider material to argue a pattern even though it cannot decide this case and RD-6's flag is not triggered by NS-2 where the GPS shows the driver was actually at the pickup.

points.response: Conceded on the location element only: GPS does put the driver 38 m from the pickup (F1) and the platform logged his arrival at 21:28:05 (F5), so NS-1(i)/(ii) are not in dispute — but D1 stops short of NS-1 because being at the pickup does not satisfy the >3-minute wait requirement.
Conceded: the "I'm Here" tap at 21:29:10 while 42 m away satisfies NS-1(i), and the driver stayed within 200 m for only 1 min 45 s after it (F6) — which is exactly why NS-1 as a whole fails.

Conceded that the arrival notice of 21:29 is documented and the chat record is complete (F9, F11); note this cuts the other way — his own notice at 21:29 and his cancellation message at 21:30 (F10) show barely one minute elapsed between announcing arrival and cancelling.

Accepted as the core of the case: on the system records the driver was within 200 m for only 2 min 50 s (F2) and cancelled 2 min 50 s after recorded arrival (F5, F4), 11 seconds short of the 3:01 required by NS-1(iii), so the condition is not literally met and the fee falls away.

Conceded on outcome: NS-2 requires the $6.61 fee be refunded in full to the rider (F7), which is what the rider asks; the rider takes no position on the driver's characterisation of his attempt beyond noting NS-2's flag condition is not met.
Agreed and adopted by the rider: the driver's "waited at least 5 minutes" statement (F12) is contradicted by F2/F3/F5 and the system records win, so it cannot support a no-show fee.

The rider does not seek a fraud flag under NS-2 (which requires the "I'm Here" tap while GPS shows the driver away from the pickup — not the case here, F1/F2/F6); the only account review sought is a profile-based one under RD-6, and that request is withdrawn so it does not distract from the refund.
Agreed: the fee charged is $6.61 with no surge (F7, F8), so the refund amount is exactly $6.61.

Agreed that no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation arises: the chat contains only an arrival notice and a cancellation notice (F9, F10), the weather was fair (F15) and no traffic incident or congestion is recorded (F13, F14).

The rider withdraws the flag_account request built on the driver's 90-day no-show history (F17); the two upheld disputes concern other trips and profile facts cannot decide this case, so the rider asks only for the $6.61 refund.

Conceded as to the arithmetic: the system record shows the driver was within 200 m of the pickup for only 2 min 50 s before cancelling (F2) and cancelled 2 min 50 s after the recorded arrival of 21:28:05 (F5, F4), which is short of the 3:01 NS-1(iii) requires, so NS-2 applies.

Conceded: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:29:10 and cancelled at 21:30:55 (F6, F4), i.e. only 1 min 45 s of in-radius waiting after his own tap, so the 3-minute threshold is not met on either measurement.

Conceded: the $6.61 fee was charged (F7, F8) and the waiting-time condition fails on the records, so NS-2 requires the full $6.61 to be refunded to the rider as a voucher under NS-7 — the driver does not contest this and asks only that it be recorded as a good-faith no-show attempt, not abuse.

Conceded: the driver's post-trip statement of a 5-minute wait (F12) is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (F3, F2, F5), and system records win over statements, so that statement is withdrawn and must not be relied on.

We accept the cancellation was the driver's, at 21:30:55 (F4); NS-0 routes this through the cancelled_by = driver branch, and since NS-1's waiting condition fails the fee is not validly incurred (F5, F2), which the driver has already conceded above.

Not contested on the merits, but it is beside the point: fair weather with no incidents or congestion (F13, F14, F15) shows only that the driver cannot invoke the RD-4 "reasonable cause" exception to route deviation, which is a route-deviation defence and irrelevant to a no-show dispute under NS-1.

The flag_account request should be refused as a rider-side demand: NS-2's account flag applies only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS shows him away from the pickup, and here GPS puts him 38–42 m from the pickup at the tap and throughout (F1, F3, F6, F2), so the abuse condition is absent; F17 is profile history about two other trips and cannot decide this case.

The two chat messages (F9, F10, F11) add nothing beyond what the GPS already shows (F2, F5): the driver's location notice at 21:29 and cancellation notice at 21:30 confirm he was genuinely present and waited, which is why the driver concedes the refund rather than contesting the delay.
